newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: EMCO welcomes NZCC ruling on NZ electricity market.
newsitem.headline: EMCO welcomes NZCC ruling on NZ electricity market.

text.p: The Electricity Market Company (EMCO) on Friday welcomed the ruling of the Commerce Commission that it had no jurisdiction over the rules for New Zealand's wholesale electricity market, due to start on October 1.

The anti-monopolies commission determined that the rules for which authorisation was sought would not lessen competition and that authorisation was neither required nor within the commission's jurisdiction.
EMCO said the new market would be vigilant in ensuring it operated in the interests of New Zealanders as a whole.
"The commission's ruling, which is very welcome, means we can complete our plans for starting the market on October 1," EMCO chief executive Lincoln Gould said in a statement.
"This will include implementing changes to the new rules which will improve the market's operating efficiency."
EMCO said the market rules included a number of safeguards designed to protect the interests of all those affected by the market, including consumers.
The commission's decision would allow the market to evolve as a result of the experiences of market participants in the new environment.
Any proposed new rule would be clearly vetted against the guiding principles built into the rules.

"A key principle is that the market functions in the interests of New Zealanders as a whole. Anyone will be able to appeal to the independent Market Surveillance Committee if they feel that any proposed new rule change would breach those guiding principles," Gould said.
